newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE NUMBER ONE FOR FOURTH CONSECUTIVE YEAR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE NUMBER ONE FOR FOURTH CONSECUTIVE YEAR.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie officially became European number one for a record-equalling fourth successive year on Sunday and immediately set himself the target of winning one million pounds ($1.57 million) for the season.

The 33-year-old Scot finished fourth three shots behind Irishman Darren Clarke after a closing seven-under-par 65 in the German Masters at Motzener See to win 32,500 pounds ($50,880) and bring his earnings for the year in Europe to 717,146.36 pounds ($1.12 million).
His only remaining counting tournament is the Volvo Masters at Valderrama later this month and victory there would make him the first player to pass the million pounds target.
"The first prize in Valderrama is 150,000 pounds ($234,800) and I get a 150,000-pound bonus for being number one, so I can get to seven figures with a victory there.
"It was my goal to pass 700,000 pounds today so that I would have the chance to go for the million and now I have done it.

"The way I am playing I can win Valderrama, though I know that it is a course that can bite you badly," said the Scot, who became the first player to head the Order of Merit four straight years since Englishman Peter Oosterhuis from 1971 to 1974.

Clarke was overshadowed by Montgomerie's achievements, but the Irishman, who had eight birdies and an eagle two at the fourth on his card, was all smiles after a superb 63 put him on 264, 24 under par. He beat Englishmen Mark Davis by one shot and Paul Broadhurst by two with Montgomerie another shot behind as he recorded his second European Tour victory.
Davis shot a best-of-the-week 62, 10 under par.
Clarke was not worried that Montgomerie had most of the publicity, saying: "Monty deserves all he gets. He is such a good player, always up there in every tournament.
"As for myself these Ryder Cup points will be invaluable. It's nice to get some on the board this year before the real battle for places starts next year."
